`@bit_bound` outside 1..32 is a front-end refusal (§7.3.1.2.1.5) and a refused file produces no octets to capture.
A writer can only set bits the bitmask declares and every one of them is below the bound; what a reader does with a bit at or above it is the read direction.

OMG IDL has no syntax that annotates a collection type, so no corpus case declares an `@appendable` or `@mutable` collection; the front ends were asked directly in the unspecified-constructs run instead.

`FLAG_2` of the extended `eMemberHeader` needs a member that is both `@must_understand` and past id 0x3F00; `annotation-must-understand` has the first and `annotation-id-sparse` the second, and no corpus case has both.
No product sets `FLAG_IMPL_EXTENSION` on a member it declares, so no capture of a writer holds one; the behaviour is what a reader does with a peer's private parameter.

The boundary is id 0x3F00 exactly and no corpus case declares it; the corpus's largest ids, 16383 and 268435455, are both past it and only show the extended form the rule sends them to. `tools/byte-gate`'s `pid_3f00` is where the boundary is measured.
The claim is that a reader accepts either header form; a writer capture shows only which form each product chose, which `annotation-id-explicit` and `annotation-id-sparse` do record.
No product writes a user member with an id in the reserved range 0x3F01–0x3FFF, so a writer capture cannot hold one; the rule is what a reader does when a peer does.
`PID_LIST_END` is what a reader must be robust to receiving; every PL_CDR1 writer here ends its list with `PID_SENTINEL`, which `struct-mutable`'s XCDR1 goldens carry.
`PID_IGNORE` says every consumer shall ignore 0x3F03; no product emits it, so there is nothing on the wire to capture.

`O.ssize` below 4 GiB is a bound on the encoding, and a payload that tested it would be over 4 GiB — every case here fits one loopback datagram.
The DHEADER a writer emits is L1; skipping an unknown tail by it is what the reader does with it.
A non-optional receiver member taking its default for an omitted mutable member is the receiver's substitution.
Skipping an unrecognised member with `must_understand = false` and keeping the sample is the reader's decision.
Discarding the sample for an unrecognised must-understand member is the reader's decision.
A reader with fewer members than the writer skipping the tail is the reader's use of the DHEADER.
A reader with more members than the writer defaulting the missing tail is the reader's substitution.
Table 9's default values appear only where a member is absent, and it is the reader that supplies them.
An explicit `@default` changes what a reader supplies for an absent member; a writer sends the sample's own value either way, which `annotation-default-value` records as M3.
A discriminator selecting a member the writer's type had no case for is a reader-side type-evolution question.
`@final` assignability is a type-compatibility rule; the mismatch is a discovery or reader verdict and not an octet.
Key members are never optional and always must-understand constrains the IDL; the front end accepts or refuses and no octet carries the constraint.
A `map` in a key is refused by every front end here; a refused file produces nothing to capture.
In a union only the discriminator may be a key is the same shape: a front-end constraint with no octets.
`DISCARD` — failing the whole aggregate for a member that cannot be constructed is what the receiver does with octets that are already correct.
`USE_DEFAULT` — the member taking its default and the aggregate surviving is the receiver's substitution.
`TRIM` — truncating an over-long string, wstring, sequence or map to what the receiver's type holds happens after the octets arrive.
`TRIM` on any other type being unspecified is a statement about the receiver's options.
The annotation's own parameter defaulting to `USE_DEFAULT` decides which of O1 to O3 a receiver applies.
The positions the annotation may appear in decide where O1 to O3 apply on the receiving side.
A map's key admits only `DISCARD` narrows the receiver's options for one position.
A discarded sample is an absence, not a decode error is the receiver's report to its own application.
